messages:
mike: Quick follow-up on the tenant-priority buckets idea from last week's RFC. I sketched a minimal plan for ownership and how it interacts with the console query surface.

tara: Nice. TL;DR?

mike: We want 3 logical priority lanes for queries: realtime, interactive, background. Each tenant gets a default bucket, but teams can opt up for dedicated realtime capacity.

sanjay: How does this map to the existing query-proxy? Are we adding flags or new routes?

mike: Minimal approach: keep one /query endpoint, add a `priority` header and a token-scoped default in the auth token. Router uses token -> tenant metadata -> bucket.

jess: Concern: authz checks currently run before routing. If we route by token metadata then calls into authz will need to be fast or cached.

mike: Agreed. Proposal: run lightweight authn to get tenant id, read tenant priority from cached config (TTL 30s). Full RBAC checks still happen at the handler, but we short-circuit heavy joins for routing decisions.

tara: That TTL feels ok but we need a clear invalidation story when we change a tenant's priority (esp during sales upgrades).

mike: Add a publish/subscribe invalidation channel from control-plane: when tenant config changes we push a small delta event to routers. Fallback is TTL expiry.

sanjay: Performance tradeoff: routing on cached tenant priority reduces tail, but if the authz cache stales we could mis-route to lower/higher capacity. Are we ok with soft staleness?

jess: For upgrades we should prefer eventual correctness. If a tenant pays for higher lane we should fast-path the invalidation (immediate push), sales ops can trigger.

mike: Exactly. Operationally: admin UI hits control-plane -> control-plane updates tenant record -> publishes invalidation to router topic. Routers update local map.

tara: Can we have a one-off admin API to force rehydrate all routers if something funky happens?

mike: Yes. `POST /admin/tenants/rehydrate?force=true` handled by a job that streams the current tenant map to all routers.

sanjay: On capacity isolation: realtime lane needs stricter SLOs. Do we plan dedicated pools or weighted shares?

mike: For now weighted shares in existing pools; Dedicated is for enterprise (reserved capacity). Weighted shares allow per-tenant `min_share` and `burst` tokens.

jess: How are limits enforced? Token bucket per-lane per-tenant in router? Or downstream executor?

mike: Router enforces admission and small prefix headroom. Execution nodes enforce throttling and queueing behavior. Two-tier enforcement to prevent head-of-line blocking.

tara: Metrics we need to add: lane admission rate, lane preemptions, queue depth per-lane, per-tenant latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) split by lane.

mike: +1. Also feature-flag rollouts: start with synthetic tenant group and internal tenants, then progressive ramp.

sanjay: Migration plan ideas? We have to map existing tenants to default lanes without affecting production.

mike: 1) Default mapping: small tenants -> interactive, high qps tenants -> background by default unless opted-in. 2) Internal tenants -> realtime. 3) Gradual traffic shadowing with `priority` header set in canary routers before enforcement.

jess: Can we do a shadow mode where routers annotate spans with `priority` decisions but don't enforce? That helps evaluate correctness and perf impact.

mike: Yup. Shadow annotation and metrics collection for 2 weeks before enforcement on each cohort.

tara: RBAC interplay: if a tenant's RBAC change removes a permission for a route used by interactive lane, we must ensure we don't send unauthorized requests to cached executors.

mike: Executors always re-check the token for route permission before executing, but we want to minimize heavy checks. So the executor will verify grant at start-of-request; router-level cache is advisory for routing only.

sanjay: What about prefix caching and KV cache coherency across lanes? If background and interactive hit same model KV cache, eviction policies differ.

mike: We'll keep a unified KV cache per-model but shard internal eviction by lane weight. Interactive lanes get preferential retention under pressure.

jess: Ops runbook for incidents: if interactive latency spikes, we should temporarily demote some big background tenants to background-throttle mode and free headroom. Can we do that automatically?

mike: We can. Implement an emergency controller that watches interactive p99 and automatically reduces `burst` tokens for background lane by calculating target throughput. Must be an opt-in safety feature and visible in console.

tara: Safety: we need guardrails so auto-demotion doesn't trigger during a monitoring blip. Use a 60s sustained breach + double-confirm via synthetic user pings.

sanjay: Security note: the `priority` header must be trusted. Only routers should be allowed to set it; any downstream service should ignore client-supplied header. Use `x-ri-priority` and drop if coming from outside.

mike: Good call. We'll normalize header at edge and inject service-signed metadata. `x-ri-priority: realtime;sig=sha256(...)` etc.

jess: Example config snippet for tenant record?

mike: ```json
{"tenant_id": "t-1234", "default_lane": "interactive", "min_share": 0.02, "burst_tokens": 2000}
```

tara: Nice. For rollout timeline: 2 weeks design + 1 week infra + 2 weeks canary shadowing + 2 weeks phased enforcement = ~7 weeks. Reasonable?

mike: Sounds right. I'll open a lightweight follow-up RFC with the sequence and the config schema.

sanjay: One more: telemetry retention. We need lane-level traces stored for 90 days to analyze regressions. That influences cost.

mike: We'll backfill high-value tenants on request; default 30 days, enterprise 90. Add opt-in extended retention flag.

jess: Any UI changes? Need a simple tenant view showing lane, current tokens, last invalidation time, and quick rehydrate button.

mike: Yep. Console team agreed to a small panel. I'll coordinate with product for a mock.

tara: I'll volunteer to own the canary plan and test harness. Sanjay can own router impl, Jess owns executor changes.

sanjay: Ack. I'll start a prototype branch for router map cache + invalidation listener.

jess: I'll draft the executor pre-check and eviction weighting changes.

mike: Thanks all. I'll post the follow-up RFC link once it's open and add action items. :thumbsup:
